forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Down 1pp to 21%. Quiet news window — Google I/O (19 May) brought Gemini 3.5 Flash and Gemini Spark agent, but neither presented as AGI; Anthropic continued rolling out autonomous managed agents in beta. State of AI May report and llm-stats confirm continued capability gains but nothing crossing the 3+ leading-researcher attestation threshold. Amodei still anchoring 2027; Hassabis maintaining ~50% by end-of-decade. Resolution mechanics remain demanding given OpenAI/Microsoft renegotiation that explicitly displaced 'AGI' with capability gates. 31 months to deadline — slow time decay continues to dominate absent fresh signal.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class — major paradigm-defining technology claims with sub-3-year horizons resolved YES historically <20%. AI Impacts 2023 survey median for HLMI clusters 2040-2047. Metaculus community currently ~25% by 2027, ~50% by 2031. Kalshi contributors put 40% on OpenAI AGI by 2030 (Jan 2026), but the resolution criterion here is broader and tougher (3+ leading researchers OR public lab announcement).

factors_up.factor: Continued frontier capability gains across labs (Gemini 3.5/Spark, GPT-5.5, Claude agentic scaling)
Amodei publicly anchoring 2027 AGI year — race dynamics may push declaration
Autonomous agent products (Anthropic managed agents, Google Spark) shorten capability-discovery loops

factors_down.factor: OpenAI removed 'AGI' clause from Microsoft contract — deprecates the term for high-stakes resolution
No researcher consensus near YES threshold; published surveys still cluster 2040+
31 months left — short relative to typical capability-to-attestation lag
Hassabis's 50% by 2030 implicitly means <50% by 2030 for stricter resolution

key_uncertainties: Whether 'AGI' as a term survives the OpenAI/MS renegotiation or fragments into capability benchmarks
Whether a lab unilaterally declares AGI for marketing/funding reasons before researcher consensus
Speed of agentic capability gains over the next 12 months
update_triggers: Any public lab claim of AGI achievement
Coordinated statement from 3+ researchers at top labs
Major capability benchmark breakthrough (e.g., METR task horizon >1 month)
Significant slowdown signal (training scaling plateau, compute constraints)

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 24%. This week's signal mixed: McKinsey continues to telegraph ~10% non-client headcount reductions over 18-24 months; KPMG cutting ~400 US advisory roles citing 'weaker market demand'; UK Big Four graduate intakes down 6-30% over two years. Offsetting: BCG reports ~$3.6B of $14.4B (25%) 2025 revenue from AI-related consulting — i.e. AI is currently additive to top-line, not destructive. Industry restructuring is real but the gap between current ~5-10% pressure and a ≥33% revenue/employment collapse by end-2030 is wide. Need either a sharp recessionary trigger or a discontinuous AI capability step that automates senior client-facing work, neither imminent.
forecasts.base_rate: Industries losing ≥33% of value/employment in ~5 years are rare absent a sector-specific disruptor (e.g. travel agents 2000-2010, video rental 2007-2013, print journalism). Professional services historically resilient because demand is partly status- and trust-driven. Reference class: 10-20%.

factors_up.factor: McKinsey 10% non-client cuts and KPMG layoffs accelerating
Sharp UK Big Four graduate hiring cuts (6-30%) — leading indicator
Junior associate billable hours collapsing under AI automation

factors_down.factor: BCG generating 25% of revenue from AI work — sector adapting, not collapsing
Trust/relationship-driven nature of senior consultancy work resists automation
5-year horizon long enough for firms to repivot to AI implementation services

key_uncertainties: Whether pricing power erodes faster than firms can repivot
Whether 'economic consultancy' is interpreted narrowly (boutique econ shops) or broadly (Big Four advisory)
Severity of any 2027-2029 macro downturn that could compound AI pressure
update_triggers: Quarterly Big Four/MBB headcount disclosures showing >5% decline
Public revenue declines >10% YoY at major firms
Industry analyst report (e.g. Source Global, Kennedy) attributing ≥20% revenue impact to AI

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 2%. YouGov 4-5 May has Reform 25%, Labour 18%, Conservatives 17%, Greens 15%, LD 14% — Labour in second on vote share, with PollCheck 7-poll average putting Labour at 18.1% behind Reform 25%. Ipsos (8-12 May) reports 74% think Starmer unlikely to win next GE; 42% think Labour would perform better with someone else. Persistent Reform lead for ~12 months, with Labour failing to recover from a 30%+ summer 2024 baseline. Next GE could be as late as Dec 2029 (3.5 years), so recovery path exists, but it would require either: a Reform implosion, a Labour leadership change followed by sustained polling rebound, or major exogenous event reshuffling the field. Probability still very low but not negligible because of horizon and FPTP swing.
forecasts.base_rate: UK governing parties trailing by 7pp at midterm have recovered to largest-party status historically <10% of the time. But Labour is starting from incumbency, with FPTP advantage in seat:vote conversion. Combine: ~3-5%.

factors_up.factor: FPTP can convert ~28% vote share into largest-party status if opposition vote fragments 4 ways
3.5 years to GE — long horizon for recovery
Reform UK's historical fragility (UKIP/Brexit Party precedent) — could collapse

factors_down.factor: 12+ months of sustained Reform lead at 25%+ — durable pattern
74% think Starmer cannot win — credibility damaged
Government unpopularity rare to fully reverse once entrenched (cf. 1992-1997 Tories)
Boundary changes since 2024 not favourable to Labour seat efficiency

key_uncertainties: Whether Starmer is replaced and by whom
Reform UK's organisational durability when scrutinised
Conservative-Reform coalition or merger possibilities
update_triggers: Labour polling >25% sustained over 3 months
Reform leadership crisis or major scandal
Snap election trigger

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 78%. ~9-year horizon means the question is dominated by base-rate AI capability trajectory rather than near-term news. May 2026 update set continues to show steady frontier gains — Gemini 3.5/Spark, Claude managed agents, GPT-5.5 cyber — consistent with prior trajectory. Hassabis ~50% by 2030 implies meaningfully higher by 2035 conditional on his model; Amodei's 2027 implies near-certainty. Most balanced view: 2035 captures both the modal expert timeline and significant capability slack. Resolution mechanics (3+ researcher attestation OR public lab announcement) less binding over 9 years.
forecasts.base_rate: Aggregated forecaster views: Metaculus community ~75-80% by 2035 (extrapolating from 50% by 2031). AI Impacts 2023 expert survey median 2047, but distribution tails imply 25-40% by 2035. Blended reference class: 60-75%.

factors_up.factor: 9-year horizon absorbs slowdowns/restarts in capability scaling
Compounding investment ($300B+ annual AI capex by 2027) maintains pace
Multiple credible labs racing — coordination failure on declaration is unlikely over 9 years

factors_down.factor: Definition drift / coordination on what counts as AGI could push declaration past 2035
Scaling plateau plus alignment/regulation constraints could delay
Energy/compute supply bottlenecks if global power buildout lags

key_uncertainties: Whether scaling laws hold for another generation
Whether geopolitical decoupling fragments compute supply
Definitional consensus on AGI
update_triggers: Capability plateau lasting 12+ months
Major compute/energy crisis
Regulatory pause across G7 economies

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 7%. AEI China-Taiwan updates through 15 May show continued grey-zone pressure (PRC research vessels mapping seabed, Transparent Ocean initiative, undersea sensor preparation) but no escalation toward overt blockade or invasion. Trump-Xi summit (13-15 May) handled Taiwan via established formula. Taiwan's special defence budget of 780bn NTD passed 8 May; HIMARS deployments to Penghu/Dongyin announced — raising costs for any PLA action. 44 months to deadline. PLA preparation continues but threshold for kinetic action remains high given economic interdependence and US deterrence posture under Trump's transactional stance.
forecasts.base_rate: Great-power-initiated kinetic conflict against a major US-aligned partner within 4-5 years: historical base rate <5%. Adjusted up for: stated CCP timeline ('readiness by 2027'), Xi's age, and rapid PLA buildup. Most expert estimates cluster 5-12% for the Trump-2 term.

factors_up.factor: Xi's stated 2027 PLA readiness target
Continued PRC seabed mapping and undersea preparation (Transparent Ocean)
Trump's ambiguous Taiwan commitments could be tested

factors_down.factor: Trump-Xi summit producing routine outcomes — no acute crisis signal
Taiwan's 780bn NTD defence budget and HIMARS forward deployment raise costs
PRC economic fragility makes kinetic disruption of trade self-defeating
No PLA mobilisation indicators or amphibious lift surge

key_uncertainties: Whether 'blockade' is interpreted strictly (>72hr per question) or loosely
How US-China relations evolve post-2026 midterms
Whether Taiwan's domestic politics provoke PRC overreaction
update_triggers: PLA reservist callup or amphibious lift mobilisation
Major US-Taiwan defence agreement upgrade
Cross-Strait kinetic incident (vessel sinking, downed aircraft)

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Up 1pp to 7%. April 2026 CPI print (released 21 May) at 2.8%, down from 3.3% in March — sharper-than-expected moderation following the 1 April energy price cap. CPIH at 3.0%, down from 3.4%. The April step-down is encouraging but the path from 2.8% to <2.0% in 7 remaining monthly prints (May-Dec 2026) is still demanding: requires sustained services disinflation while energy base effects don't reverse. Bank of England, OBR, and consensus forecasts all expect CPI to remain at or modestly above 2% through 2026. Small upward update reflects the larger-than-expected April moderation widening the tail of fast-disinflation outcomes.
forecasts.base_rate: UK CPI prints below 2% in any given month: ~30% historically, but currently in a structurally elevated regime (services CPI sticky 4-5%). Conditional on starting at 2.8% with 7 months to deadline: ~5-10%.

factors_up.factor: April 2026 surprise downside print (2.8% vs 3.3%) opens disinflation pathway
Energy price cap deflationary base effects compound through Q2-Q3
Sterling strength on monetary stance keeps imported goods in check

factors_down.factor: Services inflation still sticky 4-5% — dominant CPI component
Wage growth (RPI x ONS earnings ~4-5%) sustains domestic price pressure
Bank of England/OBR central forecasts keep CPI ≥2% through 2026
Energy reversal risk in H2 if wholesale prices firm

key_uncertainties: Whether April's 0.5pp drop reflects a one-off cap effect or a trend
Wage settlement round in autumn 2026
Imported energy and food prices through winter
update_triggers: May/June 2026 CPI print <2.4%
Services CPI print <3.5%
BoE MPC commentary signalling sub-2% expected

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 98%. Release date confirmed for 31 July 2026; trailer cumulative views now 1.1B+ (first trailer in history to cross 1B), 718.6M in 24 hours (smashed Deadpool & Wolverine record). The Numbers projection $2.54B worldwide; multiple industry models project comfortably $1B+ on logarithmic decay from opening. Comparable Tom Holland MCU Spider-Man films: Far From Home $1.13B, No Way Home $1.92B. Demand signal extraordinary. Only material downside risks are: catastrophic production/marketing event, sudden boycott trigger, or theatrical exhibition disruption — none in evidence. 5-month window from release to deadline ample for $1.5B accumulation given projected opening.
forecasts.base_rate: Tentpole MCU/Spider-Man films with $200M+ opening have crossed $1.5B globally about 35% of the time historically; conditional on trailer signal at this magnitude, base rate >90%.

factors_up.factor: Record-breaking 1.1B trailer views — first ever — extraordinary demand
No Way Home's $1.92B sets recent comparable
5-month run to deadline allows full theatrical window plus PVOD/streaming overlap immaterial to gross

factors_down.factor: China access uncertainty could lop ~$200M off worldwide gross
Tail risk of production scandal or marketing misstep
MCU fatigue could surprise to downside vs trailer signal

key_uncertainties: China release approval status
Whether trailer views translate to opening-weekend conversion
Competing Q3-Q4 tentpoles (Avengers: Doomsday adjacency)
update_triggers: Pre-sales tracking data (mid-July)
Opening weekend gross
Any production/release disruption

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 98%. April 2026 disclosures: Anthropic reported $30B ARR (some sources, e.g. Sacra, estimate up to $43B; OpenAI disputes Anthropic's gross-accounting and would put it closer to $22B net). OpenAI confirmed $24B ARR ($2B/month). Conservative (net-revenue) blend: ~$22B + $24B = $46B today, with growth rates of Anthropic ~10×/yr and OpenAI ~3.4×/yr (Epoch AI). Even a sharp slowdown to 2-3× annualised would put combined ARR comfortably above $70B by Q4 2026 (~8 months out). Generous accounting puts the combined figure near or already at $70B. Headline risk to downside: a coordinated funding/usage shock or revenue restatement. Otherwise this resolves YES on track.
forecasts.base_rate: Two specific firms achieving 50%+ combined growth from $46B in 8 months: historically vanishingly rare, but current AI infrastructure spend cycle has no precedent. Conditional on current trajectory: >95%.

factors_up.factor: Anthropic doubling every ~2 months on enterprise Claude adoption
OpenAI consumer + API revenue growing 30-40% quarterly
Even using OpenAI's lower estimate of Anthropic ($22B), the combined number is already at $46B and accelerating

factors_down.factor: Revenue-recognition disputes between companies could trigger SEC-style restatement
Major outage or trust event could compress enterprise spend
Bloomberg/FT could use stricter net-revenue definition at resolution

key_uncertainties: Which credible publication's number gets used at resolution
Whether ARR is measured at end-Q4 or as Q4 run-rate annualised
Whether either company restates upward or downward before Dec 31
update_triggers: Q2/Q3 2026 ARR disclosures from either company
Major credible-publication revenue audit
Significant enterprise contract loss

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Up 1pp to 38%. Q1 2026 GDP print of +0.6% (released 14 May) was best-in-G7 alongside US, with services sector growing 0.8% across 11 of 14 subsectors. This near-term strength doesn't directly affect 2030s averages but is consistent with a slightly improved productivity baseline. OBR March 2026 EFO still anchors at GDP per person 1.1% pa 2026-2030, TFP 1%, labour-supply growth 0.5% by 2030 — combined potential growth ~1.3-1.5%. PwC's £550B AI-by-2035 estimate suggests material productivity upside if AI diffusion accelerates. The 2030s arithmetic-mean question requires sustained ~1.5%+ growth over 10 years, which sits right at OBR potential. Small upward update reflects Q1 2026 positive surprise nudging the path probability slightly.
forecasts.base_rate: UK decadal average real GDP growth: 1980s 3.3%, 1990s 2.4%, 2000s 2.0%, 2010s 1.9%, 2020s (so far) ~1.0%. Probability of exceeding 1.5% decadal average from current trajectory: ~30-40%.

factors_up.factor: Q1 2026 +0.6% growth in line with G7 leaders — momentum carry
AI/productivity upside (PwC £550B by 2035) — could lift TFP above 1%
Capex / infrastructure pipeline (planning reform, AI compute investment) front-loaded into 2030s

factors_down.factor: OBR central forecasts at GDP per person 1.1% pa — implies headline growth ~1.3-1.5%
Ageing population reducing labour-supply growth to 0.5% by 2030
Healthcare spending crowding (8% → 9% of GDP) shifting activity to low-productivity sectors
Recession risk somewhere in the 2030s — pulls 10-year mean down

key_uncertainties: Whether UK captures AI productivity diffusion at the upper or lower end of PwC range
Migration policy trajectory and effect on labour supply
Investment response to planning reform
update_triggers: OBR upward revision of medium-term productivity forecast
Sustained quarterly GDP prints >0.5% through 2026-2027
Major AI productivity diffusion evidence in UK firm-level data
